diagram_math_checks.justification: def-fat-cantor-set defines lambda0=1 and lambda(n+1)=(lambda(n)-4^(-n-1))/2. Hence lambda1=3/8 and g0=5/8. S0 is [0,1], S1 is [0,3/8] union [5/8,1]. At scale x=8t these are exactly [0,8], [0,3], [5,8]; the omitted open middle has length 1/4.

The same recursion gives lambda2=5/32, g1=7/32. Applying the endpoint recursion to each S1 interval yields S2 intervals [0,5/32], [7/32,3/8], [5/8,25/32], [27/32,1]. Their plotted x ranges are [0,1.25], [1.75,3], [5,6.25], [6.75,8]. The two newly deleted open intervals are (5/32,7/32) and (25/32,27/32), each length 1/16, agreeing with proof step 2.1.

Every plotted S2 segment lies within an S1 segment, each S1 segment lies in S0; the displayed S2 subseteq S1 subseteq S0 is exactly the defining nested-family relation. Endpoint ticks mark included closed endpoints, consistent with def-fat-cantor-set and proof step 1.4; gaps omit interiors only. There are 1, 2, 4 retained segments respectively, independently counted in the native dark image.

The caption explicitly limits the picture to finite approximations and states proof independence. No finite drawing is claimed to establish perfection, nowhere density or the interval-cover lower bound; the unchanged numbered proof supplies those conclusions.
